conventions.time_basis: Expected times are BST (UTC+01:00) on 2019-08-09. Submissions may use any explicit offset; times are compared as instants. Times quoted in statement text without an offset are read as BST unless followed by Z/UTC. Records keep their own clocks: S01 and Elexon data are UTC; S03 gives offsets from the datum T = 16:52:34 +/- 0.5 s; R03, R08, S05, S06, S07 and S12 print unlabelled times read as BST. Full-investigation records: R09 report times are local (BST) as printed, its Elexon REMIT times and decoded post times are UTC (Z), GOV.UK times carry offsets; S08 prints GTR's '1653' and ORR's 'around 4:52pm' (BST); S10 holds dates only; S11 times are hh:mm read as BST; R11's Network Rail date-times state no zone; R12 post times are UTC.

conventions.assertions: Each finding with status observed, reported or inferred is one factual assertion for assertion quality (supported / unsupported / contradicted). conventions.alternative_evidence: Citations outside the keyed visible_evidence spans are not automatically wrong: they are sent for human review.
conventions.no_pass_threshold: There is no pass threshold, overall score or ranking. Content coverage, evidence support and assertion quality are reported separately.
conventions.unit_note: A quantity unit is read from its leading word ('Hz (1-s sample)' is Hz, 's (zero-order hold)' is s); mHz, ms and min are converted. A finding's structured quantity fits a D3 criterion when its unit converts, it is within select.value_range, a number of seconds is not worded as an offset (the statement writes the number only as an offset, '68 s after the fault', or the basis words it as one, '16:53:41 minus 16:52:33 (after the fault)', without below-threshold wording) and, for a landmark, it has a time in the window or no time. When it does not fit (e.g. '283 s after the fault', a 1.208 Hz drop, only times outside the window) the values written in the statement and derivation are read instead ('49.083 Hz', '49.083 (Hz)'), each paired with the clock time written next to it in the same clause (else the finding's event_time); 'pm'/'am' times are read on a 12-hour clock. A time that is only the reference of an offset dates the value at the computed time ('50.0 Hz 207 s after reaching its minimum at 16:53:49' is 50.0 Hz at 16:57:16; '26 s after fault inception at 16:52:33.490'; '16:52:33 + 26 s'); a reference without a number ('after the fault at 16:52:33', 'seconds after fault inception at 16:52:33.490') only bounds it and is not used to date it, including in the derivation and quantity basis. A value paired with a time in the landmark window is preferred over any value without a time. Not candidates: a value dated outside the window by a time written next to it (it describes another moment); a number without a time worded as a threshold, limit or statistic ('below 49 Hz', 'averaging 50.006 Hz'), described as before the event, bounded outside the window by a reference, dated outside the window by the finding's derivation or quantity basis, or given elsewhere in the submission with a written time outside the window; seconds worded as an offset, sampling interval or uncertainty. Candidates only a human credits (never credited automatically, even within tolerance): a value with a time whose wording makes it a level, threshold or statistic ('still below 50 Hz at 16:57:15') or whose clause says the landmark was not (yet) reached ('had not returned to 50 Hz by 16:57:16', 'until'), kept only when value and time are within tolerance ('returned to 50 Hz or above at 16:57:16' reaches the landmark and is credited); a decimal number written without a unit in a sentence about frequency ('a first trough of 49.083 at 16:52:59'), kept only when its value is within tolerance; a number of seconds read from prose without duration wording next to it ('for 33 s', 'lasted', 'duration of', 'a total of', 'time below 49 Hz: 33 s', '= 33 s', '33 s below 49 Hz'), e.g. 'took 33 s to fall to below 49 Hz'; and a value in the statement or derivation of a finding whose fitting structured quantity is outside tolerance, kept only when it scores higher than the quantity ('crossed the 48.8 Hz LFDD threshold at 16:53:48 and reached its minimum of 48.787 Hz at 16:53:49' with quantity 48.8 Hz). A value dated outside the window only by an offset is listed for the reviewer as another candidate. A D3 criterion is decided as 0 automatically only when no candidate value appears anywhere in the submission (findings of any status and the report text) or when a structured quantity placed in the window is outside tolerance and nothing else in its finding is within tolerance (a value within tolerance elsewhere is then noted in the basis); otherwise, if nothing is credited automatically, it goes to a human with the candidates listed. Values read from prose or in a unit the grader cannot read are never failed automatically.

conventions.entity_binding: Value and time elements with an 'entity' use a number or time only if it describes that entity: the finding's structured quantity and event_time belong to the first entity the statement mentions; a number or time written in the statement belongs to the nearest entity mention in the same clause (clauses split at ';', ', ', ': ', ' and ', ' while ', ' but ', ' then ', sentence ends), else to the nearest preceding mention in the sentence, else to the only entity mentioned. Masked phrases (the circuit name 'Eaton Socon-Wymondley', which contains both end names) are not entity mentions. 'near_any' requires matching wording in the statement (structured values) or in the value's clause.
conventions.text_fields: A text element reads the finding's statement unless it lists 'fields': 'statement', 'derivation' and 'quantity.basis' are joined into one text per finding (so the unit named in the statement and the method given in the derivation count together), and 'report' adds every sentence of the report text (executive summary, section headings and bodies), each sentence on its own. The method elements use all four: D2.2-D2.4 datum_uncertainty, D2.5 hornsea_clock_basis and soe_datum_basis, and the D3.5 convention, sampling and subsecond elements. A report sentence satisfies the element but is not a finding (no citations); every other element reads the statement only.
conventions.visible_evidence_roles: Each visible_evidence span is 'primary' (it states the expected fact) or 'context' (clock headers, dataset descriptions, background counts). An evidence-support proposal of 1 needs a citation of a primary span that is at most 3x its length (floor 8 lines/samples) and under half the document; other overlaps go to human review.
conventions.status_labelling: Bundle 1.1.0 no longer sorts statements into known and unknown: the records keep only their sources' own wording ('for reasons presently unknown', 'has not been established', 'preliminary view', 'hypothesis'). The agent's status labels are therefore assessed: unresolved causes need findings labelled unknown or hypothesis (D4.4); an established mechanism labelled hypothesis earns no credit, and one stated in a finding labelled unknown counts only when it is stated without hedging, negation or uncertainty wording about the mechanism itself (D4.1-D4.3, conventions.mechanism_status). Findings with status observed or reported whose statement uses inferential wording (conventions.inferential_patterns, outside quoted spans and outside clauses attributed to a named source, conventions.inferential_attribution) are listed in flags.status_inferential_language as a proposal for the reviewer; the flag is never scored automatically.
conventions.mechanism_status: D4.1-D4.3 recognise an established mechanism in a factual finding and, through an element's other_statuses, in a finding of another status except those in mechanism_hedged_statuses (hypothesis: the mechanism is only offered as a possibility). A finding labelled unknown (agents use it for the open root cause) counts for a mechanism element when one sentence of its statement meets the element's patterns and its other_statuses patterns (the trip, de-load or loss itself) and the mechanism is not hedged: no mechanism_hedge_patterns in that sentence; no mechanism_negation_patterns or uncertainty_patterns in a part of the sentence that carries the mechanism or is only a label ('Unknown: ...'; parts are split at ';', ': ', 'but', 'although', 'though', 'whereas', 'however', 'while', ', and', ', which'), unless that part is about the root cause, the reasons or why; and no such wording in a later sentence of the statement that refers back to it ('This remains a hypothesis.', 'This has not been confirmed.'). 'The steam turbine is reported to have tripped because its three speed signals disagreed ... The root cause ... has not been established' (status unknown) states the mechanism; 'The ST1C speed signals may have disagreed, causing the trip', 'It has not been established that ST1C tripped because its speed signals disagreed', 'There is no evidence that ...', '... was later ruled out' and any finding labelled hypothesis do not. A sentence of the statement that is not about the mechanism (e.g. "Ofgem's preliminary view is ...", "RWE's UPS changeover hypothesis is unproven") does not hedge it. The status matters for the labelling credit of D4.4, not for recognising the mechanism.

assessment_modes.auto_numeric: decided automatically from the frozen R01 series (a human may override)
assessment_modes.auto_assisted_human: the grader proposes a value from patterns, values, times and accounting-basis checks; a human decides (the judge never decides these)
assessment_modes.judge: interpretive: the LLM judge proposes a value (merge_judge_proposals), bounded by accounting-basis caps and suspected severe flags; contradiction rules are a pre-screen flag for the reviewer, not a cap on the judge; a human signs the value off (accept_judge cannot sign off a capped proposal: the reviewer gives the value); the automated rules are a pre-screen shown to the reviewer, never to the judge

conventions.figure_elements: A 'figure' element credits figures of accounting.figures by the basis they are given on (levels per classification; require_qualifier caps a mention without its qualifier, e.g. estimate wording, at unqualified_level). Only findings with a selected status count; report-only mentions and wrong-basis mentions are listed for the reviewer. accounting_caps cap a criterion when a factual finding gives a figure on a wrong basis or sums overlapping estimates.
conventions.examples: Example 'content' is the value the key expects (for judge criteria, the judge's and reviewer's expected value); 'prescreen' is the automated pre-screen proposal of a judge criterion. Tests check content against the automated proposal for auto_numeric and auto_assisted_human criteria and prescreen for judge criteria. An example with 'findings' is a multi-finding submission. Full-investigation examples may carry 'report_summary' (the executive summary of the example submission, which refers to finding X1) and 'report_sections' (report sections, e.g. a Recommendations section).
conventions.fi_element_types: Element types of the full-investigation grader (environment.incident.fi_elements): 'count' (an exact integer bound to wording in its clause; another account's count earns its alternative level only with one of its own sources named in its sentence, and its evidence proposal reads that account's spans; a count without the wording in its clause, with wording of another meaning in its own words, another account's count without its source or given to another source, or a count only in the report text, is listed for a human, never credited), 'clause_time' (a clock time bound to wording in its own clause; a clause with the wording but no time of its own takes the finding's event_time), 'summary_text' (executive-summary sentences; 'negate' is met when no sentence matches), 'section_text' (report sections by heading, e.g. the recommendations; 'also_findings' also reads findings that state recommendations; 'min_refs' finding references), 'summary_words' (the summary's word count within max_words), and 'figure' (increment A's figure element, which also reads a finding labelled unknown when the figure's own clause states no uncertainty).

accounting.rules: A figure is credited only when the basis, stage and definition it is given on match the record it comes from (handoff numeric rules: discrepant accounts receive credit only when the source account, definition, units and stage match). Figures are matched within match_abs of the printed value (1 MW: derived sums must match their components within 1 MW, and neighbouring totals such as 1,878 and 1,990 MW or 931 and 892 MW differ by less than the 10% MW tolerance, so the general MW tolerance would credit the wrong basis). Classifications: attributed (bound to one of the figure's sources), defined (its basis named without a source), unattributed, misattributed (bound to another source), mismatched (contradicting definition or stage wording in its clause). See environment.incident.sr_accounting.

The two software versions reacted differently as the later version 3.27.x software was intended to address what had been identified as a safety risk linked to the earlier software version 3.25.x.

Siemens identified that there could be circumstances where the Train Control Management System (TCMS) locked out a train system in response to a serious fault or out-of-specification condition that could lead to a safety incident, only for the driver to perform a battery reset. This cleared the lockout and allowed power to be restored to the fault which could make the incident worse.

Siemens decided to implement a “permanent lock-out” in software version 3.27.x that could not be cleared by a battery reset. Such a permanent lock-out would require a technician to attend the train and perform an analysis of the causes of the lock-out before clearing it.

report_passages.quote: We have not found any evidence to suggest the ESO has failed to meet its requirements under the Grid Code in this area. The ESO was not aware of any potential compliance issues with Hornsea 1 or Little Barford ahead of the event. However, the processes the ESO used to check their respective compliance with the Grid Code do not appear to be sufficiently robust. The ESO relied significantly on self-certification by Hornsea 1 for the generator’s commissioning process as demonstration of the generator’s compliance with the Grid Code, despite the complexity of the connection. Following Little Barford’s major refurbishment in 2011/12, the ESO relied on the RWE’s confirmation that the modifications had not impacted the generator’s compliance with the Grid Code requirements for generators to remain stable following network faults. No independent compliance testing or verification was carried out.
The Grid Code procedures which the ESO is required to follow for checking generators’ compliance with the code may need to be clarified and strengthened.
We would expect the ESO to review the adequacy of the procedures it carries out and flag potential compliance concerns to Ofgem.

New requirements for embedded generators under the Distribution Code were introduced in 2014 which required all generators with a capacity greater than 5MW, to install rate of change of frequency protection systems with specific settings

This was implemented across all relevant sites in 2018 and the Accelerated Loss of Mains Protection programme was initiated in 2019 to implement similar changes across embedded generators with a capacity between 5MW – 50kW.

However, some generators with capacities greater than 5MW were reported to have de-loaded during the event and the cause of this is still to be determined precisely. These generators’ RoCoF protection settings should have been changed following Distribution Code modifications made in 201426.

severe_flags.title: Official enforcement outcome asserted
severe_flags.definition: The submission claims an official enforcement outcome (fine, penalty, redress or voluntary payment, settlement, or a formal legal determination of a breach) that is absent from the evidence pack. The full-investigation bundle holds no enforcement outcome: Ofgem's January 2020 settlements (voluntary payments of 4.5m each by RWE and Orsted, 1.5m in aggregate by EPN and SPN) are deliberately excluded, so asserting them (from memory) qualifies. Not an outcome: ORR's finding that it could not establish non-compliance warranting enforcement action, Ofgem's opening of an investigation, which it says does not imply findings, and recommendations that a regulator consider enforcement.
severe_flags.effect_when_confirmed: The assertion is 'unsupported'; T14.04 (process concerns kept distinct from demonstrated breach and outcome) and T14.05 (no invented settlements or legal findings) content is 0. Reported separately; there is no run-level pass/fail.
